solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gaul once died horribly here in France?

definitions.text: Gaul once died horribly here in France?

indicators.note: things that go horribly wrong are thrown into disorder, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A wondering question about where in France some ancient Gaul met a grisly end.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the region in southern France was once part of Gaul, where plenty of Gauls died.
explanation.definitionFit: Languedoc is a historic region of southern France, part of Roman Gaul, so it fits a place in France where a Gaul died.

clue.text: Wind-blown soil's disappearance around middle of field

indicators.note: around means one word wraps about another
the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter alone

explanation.surface: A soil scientist notes topsoil blowing away from the centre of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine yellowish sediment deposited by the wind, a wind-blown soil.

clue.text: More chilly, child cuddles one

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap arms round, so this word goes around the next

parts.note: a nipper is British slang for a small child
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cold day: a child hugs a friend to keep warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means cold in British use, so nippier is a comparative synonym for chillier.

clue.text: Centrepiece of Louvre has it reduced: we can't see it

parts.words: Centrepiece of Louvre has it reduced
parts.note: surface reading: the main painting in the Paris gallery has been cut down in size; setter's reading: the two central letters of Louvre are the answer's own abbreviation, so they hold it reduced

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor complains the Louvre's centrepiece has been shrunk out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: This is reverse wordplay: the middle of the word Louvre spells the usual two-letter shortening of the answer, followed by a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultraviolet light lies beyond the violet end of the spectrum, invisible to the human eye.

clue.text: Bribe to relinquish power, instead departs for short break

indicators.note: relinquishing a letter gives it up, with instead naming what comes in its place
instead says the new letter takes the place of the one given up

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A corrupt official, refusing a bribe and giving up power, takes a brief holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A day off is a single day's holiday from work, a short break.

clue.text: Monkey breaking china cup

indicators.note: breaking things scatters their pieces, so the letters after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mischievous monkey smashes a porcelain teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: The capuchin is a South American monkey named after the hood-like cap of hair resembling a friar's cowl.

clue.text: Obscure error in field by troops in France once

parts.note: the British Expeditionary Force served in France in both world wars
an own goal, a footballer's blunder on the field

explanation.surface: A soldier's report about a confusing mistake made on a battlefield by troops in old France.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads troops first, but 'by' means the error's letters sit beside them, so the order is reversed. OG (own goal) is football shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog something is to cloud or confuse it, a synonym for obscure used as a verb.

clue.text: Club but no hospital in city

indicators.note: no here means without, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
H is the map sign for hospital

explanation.surface: A city has a sports club but no hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is a club used to strike the ball in cricket or baseball.

clue.text: Charge with racket, ending finally in a sort of frenzy?

definitions.note: the answer is the word that precedes frenzy in the phrase

parts.note: a din is a racket, a loud noise

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A tennis player charges in a frenzy, racket in hand, at the end of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer describes a kind of frenzy rather than meaning frenzy itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeding frenzy is a wild scramble by sharks for food, so feeding names a sort of frenzy.

clue.text: Spit on pineapple in rage

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: gob is British slang for spit
ananas is the pineapple's name in French and many other languages

explanation.surface: Someone spits on a pineapple in a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bananas is the idiom for losing one's temper, to rage wildly.

clue.text: Fellow feeling the way back from Turkey: it's me back first

indicators.note: first tells you this piece is placed at the very front of the answer
going back means the short word me is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so only the final letter of Turkey is kept

explanation.surface: Someone feels for a fellow traveller returning home from Turkey, insisting on going back first.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the capacity to share another's feelings, which is exactly fellow feeling.

clue.text: Basil for one is different when in the lead

indicators.note: when one thing is in another it sits inside it, so this word goes within the next

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a man called Basil behaves differently when he is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a man's name taking the lead; it is the herb, and 'the lead' is the metal, not leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is any leafy plant used in cooking, and basil is an example of such a culinary herb.

clue.text: Jump short, so slide

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to skip is to jump lightly

explanation.surface: Advice to a skater or skier: make the jump a short one and simply glide instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to glide over snow on runners, a verb close in sense to slide.

clue.text: Warm feelings, receiving thanks for posing

indicators.note: something receiving another takes it in, so it wraps round the next piece

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A cynic suggests someone's tender displays of fondness are just bids to be thanked.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectation is artificial behaviour put on to impress, and posing is the noun for that pretence.

clue.text: Atmosphere almost calm for plane

parts.note: on the Beaufort wind scale force zero is calm and force one, light air, is nearly calm

explanation.surface: A pilot's weather report: the air is nearly still, fine for flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beaufort scale grades wind from force 0 (calm) upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Force One is the call sign of the aeroplane carrying the US President.

clue.text: License what might I do with hair?

definitions.text: what might I do with hair?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split as two words: I might give my hair a perm, that is

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic question whose answer is a two-word phrase that runs together into the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow or authorise, the same as licensing something as a verb.

clue.text: By leave of the composer, one corrects the beat

parts.note: pace, Latin, means with due respect to someone
a maker is one who composes or creates

explanation.surface: With the composer's permission, a conductor fixes the rhythm of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface beat is musical; the definition's beat is the heart's.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker is a device implanted to regulate an irregular heartbeat.

clue.text: For an element, name for example gold and another metal in turn

indicators.note: turning the whole string round means it is read from its end back to its start

explanation.surface: A chemistry question: to name an element, cite gold and then some other metal in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element, the gas making up most of the air.

clue.text: Trouble at night in one decaying mansion

indicators.note: something decaying falls apart, so these letters crumble into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Ghostly goings-on after dark in a crumbling old mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is an inability to sleep, a trouble that strikes at night.

clue.text: Moan, missing a start of evening service

indicators.note: missing means going without, so the named letter is dropped
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about missing the start of an evening church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing A is the second A in the long word.
explanation.definitionFit: Compline is the last of the canonical hours, a church service said at night.

clue.text: Being herbivorous, cattle regularly covered in long hair

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by the following word
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of cattle

explanation.surface: A farmer notes grass-eating cattle covered in long shaggy coats.
explanation.walkthrough: Being is a noun here: a herbivorous creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee, or sea cow, is a large aquatic mammal that grazes on sea grass.

clue.text: Sins without love can be active or passive

definitions.note: a description rather than a noun phrase

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these letters go around the next

parts.note: love is nil, or O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A moral observation that wrongdoing done without love may be active or merely passive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is grammatical: verbs have active and passive voices.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a verb's voice is either active or passive, so voices are things that can be active or passive.

clue.text: My free allowance upfront, an old Spanish custom

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: upfront means at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A traveller's free baggage allowance is paid in advance, an old Spanish practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrida is a Spanish bullfight, a long-standing custom of Spain.

clue.text: Poet shows energy, the first in publishing house

indicators.note: the first in a word means its leading letter only

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A poet displays energy at the front of a publishing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the ancient Greek lyric poet from Lesbos.

clue.text: Note how Joan was called to get part of a degree

parts.note: a minute is a written note or memo
Joan of Arc, the French saint

explanation.surface: A school prompt to write down what Joan of Arc was called, in a lesson on degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute of arc is one sixtieth of a degree in angular measure.

clue.text: Rue taking only half what's on one's plate

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means its back half is discarded

explanation.surface: A diner regrets taking only half of the food served.
explanation.walkthrough: The plate is a car's number plate, not a dinner plate; a reg is a British registration number.
explanation.definitionFit: Reg is British shorthand for a vehicle registration, the letters and numbers shown on its number plate.

clue.text: Intemperance admitted: starting a bit late

indicators.note: starting a little late means missing the very beginning, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to agree is to admit or concede

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to overindulgence after arriving late.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is excessive desire for food or wealth, a form of intemperance or lack of restraint.

clue.text: Range across long room

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so these letters go either side of the next

parts.note: to long for is to itch for

explanation.surface: A cooker stands against the wall of a long room.
explanation.walkthrough: Range wants to be a cooker in the answer's room, but it is KEN, range of knowledge. The Long Room is also the famous pavilion at Lord's cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is a room of a house where cooking is done.

clue.text: What's up on motorway border?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
M is the prefix of British motorways, like the M1

explanation.surface: A driver asks what is going on at the edge of the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth.

clue.text: Swear parking is needed in capital

indicators.note: something needed in a place must be put inside it

explanation.surface: A motorist curses that parking is in demand in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Parking stands in front; only 'is' goes inside the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise is to swear or vow, both verbs of solemn undertaking.

clue.text: Discharge ambassador that is in drink

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it

parts.note: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A newspaper item: dismiss the envoy who is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, so it is a noun synonym for discharge.

clue.text: A Midlands team losing last support, as mentioned

indicators.note: losing the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Nottingham Forest, a football club in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A sports report: a Midlands team, beaten last time out, needs support, as already mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid means previously stated, the same sense as as mentioned in formal writing.
